card.title: THE AMERICAN GUARD
card.text: Deployment: Choose a card in hand. Convert the top card of your deck into it.
card.flavorText: The 71st New York Infantry Regiment, known as the "American Guard," boasts a storied history that stretches back to its founding in 1850. As part of the New York State Militia, the regiment served in the Civil War, the Spanish-American War, and WWI. During WWII, the 71st attached to the 44th Infantry Division, deploying to Europe in 1944. The division landed in France at Cherbourg in September 1944 and entered combat near Lunéville in October, repelling heavy German attacks in the Parroy forest. Advancing through the Vosges Mountains, the division liberated Avricourt and Strasbourg alongside French forces. In December, the 44th helped assault and capture major Maginot Line fortifications, including Fort Simserhof. After defending the Sarreguemines area through early 1945, the division crossed the Rhine at Worms in March, took Mannheim, and later crossed the Main River. In April, they pressed into southern Germany, capturing towns such as Füssen and Wertach, and pushed into Austria. On May 2, 1945, they accepted the surrender of Wernher von Braun and other German scientists. After brief occupation duty in Austria, the 44th Division returned to the US in July and was inactivated in November 1945 following the end of the war.
